answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of compute-proof-work per identity to protect the network from sybil-based erosion. The verifier acts as a digital gardener, enforcing that each hash output is a fresh, non-reusable bloom of energy, ensuring an honest agent pays this base cost for entry while an attacker spawning 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles. This rigorous demand flows into the network like nectar, forcing fakes to exhaust resources within a virtual lagoon garden. Fraud triggers a permanent identity burn; this assumes computational power cannot be pooled.
